program_sections.title: Governance, objectives and risk decisions
program_sections.content:
Proposed program policy v1.0. CISO owns the IA program, CEO sponsors it, Board approves appetite and material funding, Risk and Compliance reviews exceptions, and Internal Audit independently assesses evidence. Review quarterly and after a major event or incident.
Proposed measurable objectives for approval: preserve safe event operation; restore online entry service within its approved dependency-aware target; reject replayed tickets; review all privileged access monthly; collect evidence for every applicable control each quarter. Service owners approve numerical thresholds using capacity and exercise data.
Appetite proposal: Critical risks require immediate CISO/Operations escalation and a Board treatment decision. High residual risks need a recorded accept-or-treat decision from Risk and Compliance, with safety-affecting cases escalated to the Board. Acceptance records include owner, rationale, compensating controls, expiry and review date. No software output grants acceptance.
Exceptions are time-limited, approved by the accountable risk owner, and linked to a risk and compensating control. Change management records request, impact/safety review, test, approval, rollback and post-change validation. Vulnerabilities are triaged by exposure and safety consequence, tested before patching, and retested after deployment.

program_sections.title: Framework selection and accountability
program_sections.content:
NIST CSF organizes governance, identify/protect/detect/respond/recover outcomes. NIST RMF supplies categorize-select-implement-assess-authorize-monitor decision gates. ISO/IEC 27001 supplies the ISMS, risk treatment and statement-of-applicability process. COBIT assigns objectives, accountability and performance oversight. CIS Controls prioritizes practical safeguards. IEC 62443 defines OT zones/conduits and maintenance boundaries. NIST SP 800-82 informs OT constraints and safe change. NIST AI RMF structures Govern/Map/Measure/Manage for the crowd model and recommendation assistant. PISF 2026 provides the national benchmark mapping.
PASS is a hypothetical venue and its ownership/CII designation is unspecified. The PISF mapping is adopted as a project benchmark. Mandatory legal applicability requires confirmation of the entity's status and the official framework scope. Named framework selection does not establish certification or compliance. Control tests and evidence records support each assessment.
program_sections.source: A2 framework selection; A4 F-06/F-09; https://pkcert.gov.pk/grc-policies.asp

program_sections.title: Data protection and retention schedule
program_sections.content:
Ticket records flow from web/mobile through the application service to the spectator database and gate validation service. Payments use a provider boundary with tokenized transaction references. CCTV and sensor streams feed Physical Security; analytics outputs remain advisory. Staff/HR records use restricted corporate access. Backup copies inherit the source classification.
Apply A3 classes Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted and Critical. Display Critical as safety/operational classification alongside the separate numeric asset criticality. Encrypt sensitive transfers/storage, manage keys separately, log access and exports, and minimize fields sent to analytics or external AI.
Proposed operational retention for approval: routine CCTV 30 days, access/vendor and critical security logs 12 months, non-critical security logs 3 months, ticket/contact data 90 days after an event unless a documented business/legal need applies. These are proposed periods, subject to applicable law, payment-provider terms, claims and legal holds. Privacy Officer approves the final schedule. Deletion jobs log dataset, policy, date, count and reviewer; legal holds suspend deletion. Incident leads assess exposure and notification obligations with legal/contract owners and retain the decision record.
program_sections.source: A3 data handling; A4 F-06/F-10; final-project proposal

program_sections.title: IAM lifecycle and separation of duties
program_sections.content:
HR/business sponsor requests a named identity and role. Manager approves business access; system owner approves sensitive access; IAM provisions least privilege with MFA; SOC collects identity events. Leavers are disabled promptly and sessions/tokens revoked. Movers lose obsolete rights before new rights are granted. Temporary event staff receive event-limited accounts.
Monthly privileged and quarterly ordinary-user reviews follow A3. Vendor access requires sponsor, scoped task, start/end, MFA, VPN/jump host, session logging and immediate revocation after work. Break-glass use is time-limited, logged and independently reviewed.
Incompatible duties: access requester cannot approve their request; administrators cannot certify their own access review; developers cannot solely approve production deployment; backup administrators cannot solely approve restore evidence; AI recommendation author cannot issue risk acceptance. Operations and Physical Security approve safety-affecting changes.

program_sections.title: Dependency-aware continuity and safe operation
program_sections.content:
A3 source RTO/RPO values remain the historical baseline. Proposed recovery design first restores an isolated local entry capability, with cached signed admission data and a local anti-replay ledger, while restoring network/IAM/database services. This fallback requires proof of freshness, revocation handling, reconciliation and crowd-management approval before use. If the fallback fails validation, online gate-service recovery cannot be promised faster than its dependencies.
For CCTV/BMS, isolate compromised IT conduits at approved boundaries while retaining authorized local control, local recording and manual observation where designed. Operators preserve fire/egress functions and follow manufacturer-approved emergency procedures. The Operations incident lead and Physical Security/Facilities authorize any operational change. This project does not specify a live gate unlock or building isolation action.
Proposed protected backups use independent credentials, encryption, immutable/offline copies and isolated restoration. Replication is not a substitute for backup. Five-minute RPO requires demonstrated transaction replication or event journaling at that frequency. Measure end-to-end restore time from incident declaration to business acceptance, including dependencies, integrity checks and reconciliation.
program_sections.source: A3 recovery/IR; A4 F-04/T-04; final-project proposed design

program_sections.title: Incident command and communication
program_sections.content:
CISO leads the cyber response; Operations Director controls event-operation decisions; Physical Security and Facilities control their safety procedures. SOC triages and records the incident timeline. IT isolates affected business endpoints, preserves evidence, restores from clean sources and validates identities before reconnection.
Proposed severity scheme: SEV1 safety exposure, significant spectator-data compromise or loss of a critical event service; SEV2 contained material service compromise; SEV3 limited lower-impact incident. SOC immediately calls CISO and Operations for SEV1 and uses a 15-minute internal escalation target for exercises. Management approves external communications; Privacy/Legal evaluate notification duties. Avoid attributing a legal reporting deadline without a verified obligation.
Communication template records confirmed impact, affected services, protective instructions, current workaround, next update time and approved spokesperson. Preserve original evidence, cryptographic hashes, collection time/timezone, collector, transfer history and restricted access. Lessons produce linked corrective actions, risk reassessments and verification dates.
program_sections.source: A3 ransomware scenario; A4 F-04/F-13; final-project proposal

program_sections.title: SOC architecture and monitoring plan
program_sections.content:
Sources include endpoint/EDR, email, IAM/PAM, VPN/jump hosts, firewalls, cloud audit, ticketing and database export logs, POS management, CCTV administration, BMS gateways, IoT device identity and backup jobs. Where OT devices cannot export safely, use approved passive/gateway collection. Normalize events, synchronize clocks, send through protected collectors to SIEM, enrich and correlate, then route incidents to SOC and CISO/Operations.
Test cases cover privileged-login anomalies, replayed tickets, unusual exports, guest-to-OT denials, expired vendor sessions, failed/altered backups and model-input integrity alerts. Each rule records source, owner, expected alert, triage action and false-positive review. Monitor source heartbeat, dropped events and storage. Daily source health and monthly sample alert tests supplement event-day checks. SOAR may group/enrich/route alerts; containment and safety changes require authorized humans.
program_sections.source: A3 monitoring; A4 F-13 and missing BMS/CCTV/POS sources

program_sections.title: Cloud and IoT/OT security architecture
program_sections.content:
Separate public/guest access, externally facing applications, corporate services, payment systems and OT/safety zones. Use default-deny conduits and approved application/API paths. Public Wi-Fi cannot route to corporate or OT management. Vendor maintenance terminates at an MFA-protected jump host with task approval and session expiry.
Cloud responsibility matrix: provider supplies contracted infrastructure protections; PASS owns identity, workload configuration, data classification, encryption/key decisions, backup validation and incident integration; SaaS responsibilities follow the service agreement. Review public storage, privileged grants, secrets and configuration drift.
IoT inventory records device owner, firmware version, support end date, device identity, approved protocol and maintenance window. Authenticate devices, validate telemetry freshness, encrypt supported links and isolate unsupported devices with compensating controls. Facilities approves OT patches and rollback after representative lab tests. Maintain local operational procedures for network/provider loss.

program_sections.title: AI governance and model inventory
program_sections.content:
Inventory both systems: A16 crowd prediction and the local PASS risk/control assistant. Record model/rules version, training/reference source, owner, data classification, purpose, permitted outputs, provider and review date. Crowd-model version/vendor details require supplier confirmation. The assistant uses the versioned local control catalog and optional validated LLM ranking.
Hallucination: restrict recommendations to catalog IDs and check output. Bias: review per-scenario error rates. Leakage: use synthetic/minimized inputs; approve external providers and retention. Prompt injection: treat text as untrusted, allow no tool execution, validate IDs. Drift: rerun a fixed benchmark after catalog/provider changes. Over-reliance: require human verification and separate approval. Explainability: expose matching risk, rationale, framework and evidence. Availability: offline local mode and manual review. Vendor risk: version/change review, incident notice, exit plan and revalidation.
CISO owns the assistant; Privacy approves data use; Risk and Compliance approves governance changes. Crowd guidance is advisory to Physical Security. High-impact decisions, certification, risk acceptance and live operational changes remain accountable human decisions.
program_sections.source: A1 R16; A4 F-08; project AI requirement

program_sections.title: Exercise calendar and acceptance criteria
program_sections.content:
Before each major event: Operations checks contacts, fallback documents, backup status and local control availability. Monthly: IT performs a sampled isolated restore and privileged-access review. Quarterly: SOC replays labeled test events, owners review evidence, and Risk and Compliance reviews open High risks and exceptions. Twice yearly: cross-functional DR and ransomware tabletop including Operations, Physical Security, Facilities, Privacy and key suppliers. Annually: independent audit, BIA refresh and supplier reassessment.
Each exercise records objective, participants, scenario, start/end, observed RTO/RPO, integrity checks, pass/fail, evidence IDs and improvement owners. Pass requires business acceptance, safe operation, approved target attainment and accurate reconciliation. A failed criterion creates or updates a finding and linked risk. Closure requires a repeated successful test and independent reviewer sign-off. No exercise is claimed as completed in the source assignments.
program_sections.source: A3 monthly/twice-yearly schedule; A4 F-13; final-project test design

program_sections.title: Illustrative PKR business case
program_sections.content:
Classroom planning assumptions for one year, pending Finance approval and supplier quotations. Three independent loss scenarios are assumed: privileged compromise asset value PKR 10,000,000, exposure factor 0.20, ARO 0.30; ransomware PKR 8,000,000, EF 0.30, ARO 0.25; spectator breach PKR 6,000,000, EF 0.25, ARO 0.20. Their SLE values are PKR 2,000,000, 2,400,000 and 1,500,000; ALE values are PKR 600,000, 600,000 and 300,000. Total illustrative ALE is PKR 1,500,000 per year.
Assume respective post-control ALE of PKR 300,000, 240,000 and 150,000, totaling PKR 690,000. Estimated annual benefit is PKR 810,000. Proposed annualized control costs are PKR 180,000 for MFA/PAM, PKR 220,000 for backup/EDR, and PKR 100,000 for data access/export controls, totaling PKR 500,000. BCR is 810,000/500,000 = 1.62. ROSI is (810,000-500,000)/500,000 = 62%.
Scenarios may overlap; the example assumes no shared incident losses. Finance must de-duplicate scenarios and validate frequencies, costs and useful lives. Life safety and binding duties can justify controls irrespective of BCR. These monetary estimates are independent of the ordinal 1-25 risk scores.

program_sections.title: Three-year future readiness
program_sections.content:
Year 1 establishes the five registers, ownership, applicable obligations, MFA, segmentation, safe fallback design and baseline testing. Priority milestones are 30-day evidence collection/audit coverage, 60-day approved treatment/privacy/recovery design, and 90-day costed board decisions plus re-audit. Milestones are relative to an approved project start; source audit date conflicts prevent inferring calendar deadlines.
Year 2 expands measured recovery, passive OT telemetry, supplier assurance, model-performance monitoring and repeatable evidence collection. Compare pre/post control tests and track exception age and remediation results.
Year 3 integrates continuous assurance and cryptographic inventory, identifies long-lived sensitive data and public-key dependencies, evaluates supplier post-quantum roadmaps, and tests migration in a non-production environment. Adopt algorithms and deadlines only after verifying current national/vendor guidance and compatibility. Reassess the roadmap annually with ownership, evidence and funding decisions.
program_sections.source: Project three-year roadmap; A1 future challenges; A4 corrective actions

program_sections.title: Source discrepancies and scope
program_sections.content:
A4 cover dates the audit 24 October 2026, while test/closing sheets use 13 October and Assignment 3 is listed as 14 October. Preserve all reported dates; ask auditors to confirm chronology before calculating calendar due dates. A4 records 44.46/100 and an insufficient-assurance conclusion in the executive text, while a closing checkbox selects Partially effective. Under the report's own scale, 44.46 is Insufficient; display the conflicting checkbox as a source discrepancy.
A4's 39.1% is planned ordinal risk-score reduction across 15 treated risks (220 to 134). Its 33.3% is weighted heat-map readiness, distinct from the course's satisfied/applicable compliance ratio. No Critical findings were reported, while F-04 is High and priority safety escalation. The three Critical risks and High findings are different populations.
The reviewed baseline contains 16 assets and 16 risks. Preserve IDs, source recovery targets and source planning estimates; track final-project additions with separate provenance. Audit conclusions cover classroom documents and do not certify live control operation.

program_sections.title: Additional risk scenarios and preliminary scoring
program_sections.content:
The original 16-risk register remains the assignment baseline. The following proposed scenarios extend scope and require owner validation before incorporation into the approved baseline. Scores use the same L x I model and are planning judgments, not measured frequencies.
PR17 Mobile API account abuse: A03, weak session/object authorization; L3 x I4 = 12 High. Digital Services owner tests session expiry, access checks and export limits; require application test evidence.
PR18 Public Wi-Fi abuse or pivot: A10/A09, weak isolation and unmanaged devices; L3 x I4 = 12 High. Network owner verifies guest isolation and response logging.
PR19 Insider or temporary-staff misuse: A13/A04, excessive event access; L3 x I4 = 12 High. CISO/HR validates time-bound roles, supervision and leaver removal.
PR20 Gate/power/network failure during emergency movement: A01/A09, common dependencies or missing safe operating arrangements; L3 x I5 = 15 High with priority safety escalation. Operations and competent safety specialists validate approved emergency procedures, resilient power and a controlled exercise.
PR21 Video-analytics privacy or subgroup bias: A16/A06, excessive collection and uneven model performance; L3 x I4 = 12 High. Privacy/Physical Security review data minimization and representative error rates.
PR22 AI assistant prompt injection or leakage: recommendation workflow, untrusted input and external-provider data handling; L3 x I4 = 12 High. CISO tests allowed IDs, no tool execution and synthetic/minimized external inputs.
PR23 Cloud/provider outage or model change: A12/A16, concentrated dependency; L3 x I4 = 12 High. CIO validates recovery/export capability and version-change regression tests.
Treatments are proposed, residual L/I remain unassessed, and no acceptance decision is implied.
